subject: Request to pause trial countdown while procurement completes
messages:
From: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@clearmindhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clearmindhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial access - request to pause countdown while PO clears

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday — the demo went well. We're about to route a PO and finalize the vendor insurance checks, but Finance told me the procurement approval window might slip into next week. Our security/compliance team has requested an updated certificate from our insurance provider which is delaying the formal PO issuance.

Could Redwood pause the trial countdown (or grant a short buffer of credits) until our PO is final? We need to keep the sandbox live for the integration team to finish the validation tests. If a formal pause isn't possible, a 7-10 day temporary token top-up would also work.

Attachments: insurance_certificate.pdf (current copy)

Appreciate any flexibility — we really want to move this to a pilot but don't want the window to expire while procurement catches up.

Best,
Rajiv
VP of Engineering
Clearmind Health
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@clearmindhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial access - request to pause countdown while PO clears

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the note and for sharing the certificate.

We can do one of two things quickly:

1) Freeze the trial countdown for up to 10 calendar days while your PO and insurance verification complete (no usage credits consumed during the freeze).
2) Issue a one-time 7-day token top-up equivalent to ~25k tokens so your team can finish verification tests while procurement finishes.

Option 1 is our cleaner choice operationally; option 2 is slightly faster if you need immediate runtime. I’ve looped in David (CS) and Kimberly (Finance) for approval on the freeze. If you can confirm which you'd prefer and share an estimated PO finalization date, I’ll action it today.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial access - request to pause countdown while PO clears

Avery — finance is OK with a 10-calendar-day freeze for CLMD-2026-57 as a one-off, provided procurement sends a PO scan or DocuSign stub once available so we can tie the extension to the account. Please note we'll log the freeze in the billing system as a temporary suspension (internal note attached).

Attachment: PO_status_snapshot.png (internal reference)

David, can you confirm the operational steps to pause the trial so we don't accidentally bill during the window?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Finance Operations
From: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@clearmindhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clearmindhealth.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial access - request to pause countdown while PO clears

Avery — that would be fantastic. Please proceed with the 10-day freeze starting now. We expect the PO to be routed by 2026-07-20 pending final insurance confirmation. I’ll forward the signed DocuSign stub as soon as procurement shares it.

Really appreciate the help — this keeps our integration sprint on track.

Best,
Rajiv
